transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~39 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Priya (Aurelia CTO), Liam (Aurelia ML Eng), Karen (Aurelia SRE)
Shared links: pilot-results.csv (in drive), live dashboard (redwood-console link), security-summary.pdf

Summary:
Quick sync on pilot throughput tuning; review last week's benchmark, investigate intermittent queueing/backpressure spikes, decide on next benchmark knobs (concurrency, batching window, queue depth), and agree next steps for 1-hour steady-state run.

Topics:
- Continuous batching behavior at different concurrency targets
- Observed backpressure spikes when KV cache cold starts
- Queue depth and retry/backoff interplay with SLOs
- Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, accept rate, queue depth, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining we got about 40 minutes. quick readout from elena then open floor.
[00:18] Elena: hi all, i pulled the run from yesterday right, the 30m from 11/6. so summary - steady state looks good at lower conc but we hit a few spikes around 14:20 UTC, queue depth jumped, batching collapsed briefly.
[00:32] Priya: when you say collapsed, does that mean the runtime stopped batching or batches were tiny?
[00:39] Elena: yeah batches dropped to single-digit tokens per batch for a minute, so throughput dropped; looks like a KV cache miss storm coincident with a spike in long-context calls.
[00:53] Liam: we did release a new prompt variant that includes full patient history in ~1.6k tokens, might explain it. most calls are 128-256 but ~8% are long.
[01:05] Karen: from infra side we saw some retry storms, the client did a 500ms backoff but multiple clients retried in a window. that amplified queueing.
[01:18] Samir: ok that tracks. two levers: increase concurrency so runtime can keep batching even when some calls are long, and tune continuous batching window to avoid tiny batches. also consider prefix priming for KV cache.
[01:33] Priya: what's the risk of raising concurrency? p50 might be fine but p99 could worsen?
[01:38] Elena: correct, there's a sweet spot. in internal tests, moving from conc 24 to 48 increased throughput by ~1.8x but p99 increased ~30ms; acceptable if your p99 SLO is 500ms.
[01:50] Liam: our current SLO target is p95 < 350ms, p99 < 700ms for interactive flows. background tasks can be higher.
[02:02] Samir: noted. so proposal: run 1-hour at concurrency=48, continuous batching window set to 30ms (was 15ms), queue depth cap at 512, and enable prefix caching for frequent prompts. collect batch size histogram and KV hit-rate.
[02:19] Karen: can we also capture client-side retry timings and status codes? we need to see if 429s are from throttling or queueing timeouts.
[02:26] Elena: yes we'll instrument client tracer and capture 429 vs 5xx.
[02:29] Priya: during the spike, did you see any GPU saturations?
[02:34] Elena: gpu utilization stayed around 70-85%; not fully saturated. the bottleneck looked transient in the scheduler caused by a flurry of long contexts serializing cache population.
[02:46] Liam: would quantizing model help? we are using 8-bit now; we can test q4 if needed but prefer to solve batching first.
[02:55] Samir: agreed — quantization is a separate axis. for this pilot focus on batching/concurrency/priming.
[03:02] [03:02] Samir: ok elena can you walk through the dashboard numbers real quick?
[03:07] Elena: sure, pulling up the dashboard link. so p50 ~110ms, p95 ~320ms, p99 ~620ms for the 30m run. average batch size was 6 at conc24, avg batch size dropped to 2 during the spike. kv cache hit rate overall 78% but during the spike it went to 12%.
[03:26] Priya: 12% wow. that's the miss storm. how many distinct prefixes?
[03:30] Elena: about 4.2k unique keys in that window, a lot of slightly different patient IDs and timestamps.
[03:37] Liam: we can canonicalize prompts to reduce uniqueness, i can run a script to normalize IDs before sending.
[03:43] Karen: that will help. also we might want a short-lived LRU prime for common prefixes.
[03:49] Samir: good ideas. on queueing policy — right now we accept up to queue depth 1024 and backpressure kicks in with 429 after 800. we can lower the accept window to 512 and have earlier 429s to avoid long tail retries.
[04:03] Priya: would that cause poorer client experience? we prefer slower instances to 429 bursting.
[04:08] Samir: tradeoff. earlier 429s cause clients to backoff gracefully rather than retry immediately into the queue. if clients do exponential backoff with jitter it's smoother.
[04:17] Liam: current client lib uses fixed 500ms backoff for 3 retries, then fail. we can change to exp backoff.
[04:22] Karen: we'll update client soon.
[04:25] Samir: ok timeline wise elena will run the 1-hour steady-state at conc48 with batch window 30ms and queue cap 512. also enable priming for top 100 prefixes. collect pilot-results.csv with per-minute metrics.
[04:39] Elena: noted. i'll also dump batch size distribution and the raw kv miss events.
[04:45] Priya: what about canary/fallback? if p99 degrades we should fallback to a smaller model variant with lower latency.
[04:52] Samir: yes we have an automatic fallback policy — canary at 5% traffic to smaller variant. we can expand to 10% if you'd like.
[05:00] Priya: start with 5% then see.
[05:03] Liam: also let's capture sequence length distribution per-minute; that will show correlation with KV misses.
[05:09] Elena: good call.
[05:12] [05:12] -- interruption --
[05:15] Karen: quick ops note, we saw an event where the autoscaler added a node but traffic routing lagged ~20s causing a small spike. might be separate but worth noting.
[05:24] Samir: thanks, we'll correlate timestamps.
[05:27] Priya: can you also share the billing estimate for conc48 for a month? we need to model costs if we go Dedicated.
[05:33] Samir: sure i'll attach a cost sheet and a couple of commit tier options.
[05:36] Priya: perfect.
[05:38] Elena: i'll run the benchmark tonight and share pilot-results.csv and a short notes doc.
[05:44] Samir: great. any blockers from your side, liam?
[05:48] Liam: i'll produce the 1k prompt set and canonicalization script by Sunday. also will instrument client for exp backoff.
[05:55] Priya: for security/compliance, we'll need to see audit logs for the pilot. can you send the retention policy?
[06:01] Samir: yes security-summary.pdf in the drive has retention and KMS notes. i'll re-share with audit log excerpt.
[06:08] Karen: also SSO/SCIM is something we'll want before Dedicated ramp. follow-up later.
[06:13] Samir: noted.
[06:15] Priya: last question, what's your recommendation for concurrency ceiling? 64? 96?
[06:21] Elena: depends on model and GPU type. for your model and the instance family in the pilot, i'd cap at 64 as a safety limit. beyond that we saw diminishing returns and p99 jumps.
[06:32] Liam: ok 64 cap sounds fine.
[06:35] Samir: to recap next steps: Elena run 1h at conc48, collect metrics; Liam share prompts and update client backoff; Samir send cost/commit options and audit logs; schedule kv priming deep-dive next Tue.
[06:50] Priya: sounds good. thanks all.
[06:53] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in slack and with the deck. meeting adjourned.

Post-meeting notes:
- Instrumentation to include per-batch token count, batch latency, and KV miss stack traces for the 1-hour run.
- Action items copied to CRM.
- Next sync: tentative Tue 2025-11-11 for deep-dive, will confirm via calendar.
